pages.title: Adjusting the Weights
pages.text:
Adjusting the Weights
• Eventually, error (E) is a function of the weights and the inputs.
– Why not just express E, in terms of w’s and x’s and minimize it ?
• For a network of decent size and non-linear transfer functions, expressing E analytically in terms of weights and minimizing it becomes tedious and almost impossible.
• Neural networks with just input and output layers (no hidden layers) are very limited in what they can do and they need carefully crafted features, which are tedious to get.
• Neural networks with many hidden layers (deep neural nets), can learn features without much human intervention.
• So, we use numerical methods to adjust the weights.
– Gradient decent is a popular choice
